findings.title: Pause and Delete menu actions become unreachable for Grafana rules rendered by the new ruler-less list view
findings.body: The Pause menu item (line 123) is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is true, and the Delete menu item (line 165, `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}`) is only rendered when `rulerRule` is truthy. Both require an actual `RulerRuleDTO`. However, the new Grafana-only alert list rendering path (`GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`) never supplies `rule`/`rulerRule` to `AlertRuleMenu` — it only passes `promRule` (a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`), since this PR's goal is to stop fetching ruler data for this view. `canPause`/`canDelete` were updated to also become true from the new prom-based ability checks (`grafanaPauseAbility`/`grafanaDeleteAbility`), but the JSX gating conditions were not updated to match, so Pause and Delete will never render for rules shown in this view even when the user has full permissions. This silently removes two previously available actions from the alert list's dropdown menu. The regression is masked rather than caught by `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`'s 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' test, which grants delete/update permissions yet asserts exactly 4 menu items (Silence, Copy link, Duplicate, Export) with no Delete or Pause entries.

findings.title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem breaks React list identity in the filtered rule list
findings.body: In the `rules.map()` render loop, the `'datasource'` and `default` cases still pass `key={key}` to their returned elements, but the `'grafana'` case's `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` lost its `key` prop entirely (the previous implementation using `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>` had it). This produces React 'missing key' warnings and risks incorrect component reuse/state across re-renders for Grafana rule items in this list, which is populated incrementally via infinite scroll (new batches pushed into `rules` state). The pre-computed unique key from `getRuleKey`/`getGrafanaRuleKey` should be applied here just like the sibling cases.

findings.title: Rule view link no longer includes the `returnTo` query parameter
findings.body: The view URL is built as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` without a `returnTo` parameter. The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx` built the equivalent link with `createRelativeUrl(path, { returnTo })` where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()`. Since this new component is used both by `FilterView.tsx` and `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` to render every Grafana rule link in the alert list, clicking through to a rule's detail/view page from the list now loses the information needed to return back to the originating list/filter, regressing the previous 'go back' navigation behavior.

findings.title: Stale JSDoc still references the Ruler response this component no longer queries
findings.body: The `expectedRulesCount` prop's doc comment states: "Ruler response might contain different number of rules, but in most cases what we get from Prometheus is fine", implying the component still cross-checks against a ruler response. This PR removes the `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` call entirely (the component now exclusively calls `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery`), so the comment is now inaccurate and should be updated to avoid confusing future maintainers about the component's actual data sources.

findings.title: Ability hooks are now invoked twice per rule regardless of relevance, doubling permission-check overhead
findings.body: `AlertRuleMenu` now unconditionally calls both `useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, groupIdentifier, [...])` (lines 57-64) and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(... , [...])` (lines 67-79) for every rendered rule, even though in the new ruler-less list view `rulerRule` is always `undefined` and the ruler-based branch is a no-op. Each of these aggregate hooks internally invokes several other hooks (`useIsRuleEditable`/`useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, `useFolder`, `useCanSilence`/`useCanSilenceInFolder`, `useAlertingAbility`), so this roughly doubles the hook computation performed per rule row. Since existing comments in this codebase already flag that these ability hooks are 'called a lot... for ~80 rules' and this PR's stated purpose is to make the list scale better by removing extra requests, unconditionally evaluating both ability branches for every row works against that goal.
